idiom_name: kotlinx.coroutines: Flow.timeout(silenceBudget) over an arrival flow (withTimeout for a single suspend point)
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the detection mechanism as a library operator: model arrivals as a Flow (or Channel.receiveAsFlow) and apply Flow.timeout(budget), which fails the collection with TimeoutCancellationException when no item arrives in time - that exception is the absence alarm, and catch/onCompletion carries the escalation. For a single suspend point (a queue receive, a poll call) withTimeout(budget) does the same job without a flow. Structured concurrency then ties the monitor to its scope, so a cancelled service stops monitoring instead of paging during shutdown; what remains hand-written is the per-subject expectation registry and the alert state machine (debounce, repeat, clear).
pitfalls: Flow.timeout is per-collector: cancelling one collection does not mean the flow is globally silent, so a monitor and a business collector on the same SharedFlow see different timeouts - monitor a dedicated hot flow or a shared state.
catch { } swallows CancellationException and can hide shutdown; rethrow anything that is not the TimeoutCancellationException you are handling.
A watchdog coroutine launched in a scope that is never cancelled keeps running (and alerting) after the service stops; tie it to the service lifecycle rather than to a global scope.
withTimeout must not wrap work that mutates shared state: the timeout cancels the coroutine, and a partially applied update can leave the alert state inconsistent.
